'''Erick M. Carreira''' (born 1963) is a Cuban-born American [[organic chemist]] and professor at [[ETH Zürich]]. He is known for his research group's work in [[total synthesis]] projects, particularly [[asymmetric synthesis]] of complex [[natural product]]s.<ref name="ethbio">{{cite web|title=Carreira, Erick M., Prof. Dr.|url=http://www.carreira.ethz.ch/the-group/people/prof-dr-erick-m-carreira.html|website=ETH Zurich|accessdate=13 March 2017}}</ref><ref name="ethresearch">{{cite web|title=Research - Carreira Research Group|url=http://www.carreira.ethz.ch/research.html|website=ETH Zurich|accessdate=13 March 2017}}</ref> He became the [[editor-in-chief]] of the ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]'' in 2021.<ref name="axial_2020">{{cite web |last1=Stanchak |first1=Jesse |title=Erick Carreira to Serve as Next JACS EIC |url=https://axial.acs.org/2020/09/03/erick-carreira-next-jacs-eic/ |website=ACS Axial |date=3 September 2020 |publisher=American Chemical Society |access-date=28 December 2020}}</ref><ref name="jacs_editors">{{cite web |title=Editors & Editorial Board |url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/jacsat/editors.html |website=Journal of the American Chemical Society |access-date=7 January 2021}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Carreira was born in 1963 in [[Havana]], Cuba. He received his [[B.S.]] in 1984 from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]], where he worked with [[Scott E. Denmark]]. He then began graduate work at [[Harvard University]] as a student of [[David A. Evans]] and received his [[Ph.D.]] in 1990. He was a [[postdoctoral fellow]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]] with [[Peter Dervan]] until he joined the faculty there in 1992.<ref name=ethbio />

==Academic career==
Carreira began his independent research career on the Caltech faculty and became a [[full professor]] in 1997. While there, he received several awards for successful new faculty and for his skilled teaching. He has been a full professor of chemistry at [[ETH Zürich]] since 1998.<ref name=ethbio />

Carreira has coauthored and coedited several major reference works in the total synthesis field,<ref>{{cite book|last1=Carreira|first1=Erick M.|last2=Kvaerno|first2=Lisbet|title=Classics in stereoselective synthesis|date=2008|publisher=Wiley-VCH|location=Weinheim|isbn=978-3-527-32452-1|edition=1. Aufl.}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Carreira|first1=Erick M.|last2=Yamamoto|first2=Hisashi|title=Comprehensive chirality|date=2012|publisher=Elsevier|location=Oxford|isbn=978-0080951676}}</ref> including volume 93 of ''[[Organic Syntheses]]''.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Davies|first1=Huw M. L.|last2=Carreira|first2=Erick M.|title=Organic Syntheses, Volume 93|date=April 2017|publisher=Wiley|isbn=978-1-119-34902-0}}</ref> In 2019, Carreira was appointed as the editor-in-chief of [[Organic Letters]] published by the [[American Chemical Society]], where he had previously served as an associate editor for 18 years.<ref>{{cite web |title=Carreira Next Editor-in-Chief of Organic Letters|date=October 2018 |url=https://axial.acs.org/2018/10/01/erick-m-carreira-eic-organic-letters/ |accessdate=13 May 2020}}</ref> In April 2020, Carreira was elected for a membership in the [[National Academy of Sciences]] of the United States.<ref>{{cite web |title=National Academy of Sciences Elects New Members |url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2020-nas-election.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200428010617/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2020-nas-election.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 28, 2020 |accessdate=13 May 2020}}</ref> In September 2020, he was appointed chief editor of the ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]''. Carreira is the first Hispanic American scientist to hold the position.<ref name=cen>{{cite news |last1=Wang |first1=Linda |title=Erick Carreira named editor in chief of JACS |url=https://cen.acs.org/acs-news/publishing/Erick-Carreira-named-editor-in-chief-of-JACS/98/web/2020/09 |accessdate=September 18, 2020 |work=Chemical and Engineering News |date=September 3, 2020}}</ref>

===Carreira letters===
The appointment reignited debate over a 1996 letter in which Carreira highlighted his expectations for long working hours in his research group, which were viewed as inappropriately demanding and demeaning by other professors.<ref name=cen /> In response, Carreira released a statement disavowing the approach reflected in the letter.<ref name=cen /><ref name="twitter">{{cite web |last1=Carreira |first1=Erick |title=JACS Statement |url=https://twitter.com/J_A_C_S/status/1302240951474294787 |publisher=Twitter |access-date=28 December 2020}}</ref> Carreira began his appointment in January 2021, succeeding [[Peter Stang]].<ref name="axial_2020" /><ref name=jacs_editors /><ref name=cen /> Carreira also wrote a letter in 1999 highlighting expectations for the scheduling of a student's thesis defense and non-permanence of PhD completion scheduling at Carreira's sole discretion. The terms of Carreira's request included restriction of all vacation time during the thesis writing process and held the student accountable for financial liabilities such as "rental agreements [and] airline change fees" incurred should Carreira decide that he needed to change the date of the defense . This letter was also published in response to Carreira's appointment to his JACS position.<ref>{{cite web |title=Erick Carreira JACS EIC |date=7 September 2020 |url=https://www.reddit.com/r/Chempros/comments/iodafs/erick_carreira_jacs_eic/ |publisher=Reddit |access-date=3 May 2022}}.</ref>

==Research==
Research in Carreira's group focuses on [[total synthesis]], particularly [[asymmetric synthesis|asymmetric]] (that is, [[enantioselective]]) synthesis of complex [[natural product]]s. The group also works on applications of these methods to development of [[catalyst]]s and to [[medicinal chemistry]].<ref name=ethresearch />

==Awards and honors==
* [[Beckman Young Investigators Award]], 1993<ref name="Beckman">{{cite web |title=Erick M. Carreira |url=http://www.beckman-foundation.org/beckman-young-investigators/erick-m-carreira |website=Arnold and Mabel Beckman Foundation |accessdate=1 August 2018}}</ref>
* Fresenius Award, [[Phi Lambda Upsilon]], 1996<ref name="fresenius">{{cite web|title=Award Recipients|url=http://philambdaupsilon.org/national-fresenius-award/award-recipients/|website=Phi Lambda Upsilon|accessdate=14 March 2017}}</ref>
* [[American Chemical Society]] Award in Pure Chemistry, 1997<ref name="acs">{{cite web|title=ACS Award in Pure Chemistry|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/acs-award-in-pure-chemistry.html|website=American Chemical Society|accessdate=14 March 2017}}</ref>
* Thieme-[[IUPAC]] Prize, 2002<ref name="ci">{{cite journal|title=Awards and honors|journal=Chemistry International|date=2002|volume=24|issue=3|page=14|url=https://www.degruyter.com/downloadpdf/j/ci.2002.24.issue-3/ci.2002.24.3.14a/ci.2002.24.3.14a.pdf}}</ref>
* [[Ryoji Noyori Prize]], 2021<ref>{{cite web |title=Ryoji Noyori Prize |url=https://www.ssocj.jp/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Noyori%20announcement2021-2.pdf |access-date=7 March 2022}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
He has always enjoyed animals and owns 15 birds.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-10-01 |title=Erick M. Carreira Will Be the Next Editor-in-Chief of Organic Letters |url=https://axial.acs.org/2018/10/01/erick-m-carreira-eic-organic-letters/ |access-date=2022-04-29 |website=ACS Axial |language=en-US}}</ref>
